reactor_type: stainless steel chamber with an 11.4-cm-diameter heated area and an 11.4-cm aluminum RF electrode
evidence: The PEALD process with low-reactivity oxidants is simpler than a conventional ALD process. Undoped ZnO films are deposited layer by layer by first providing a pulse of a metal–organic precursor, typically diethylzinc (DEZ), purging the excess precursor using the weak oxidant, pulsing the RF plasma to oxidize the absorbed zinc precursor, and finally purging the precursor gas-phase reaction products using the weak oxidant. This constitutes one cycle and is repeated to deposit thin films. An example cycle used was a 2-s DEZ pulse, a 4-s purge with N2O, a 2-s plasma, and a 4-s purge with N2O.
